messages:
devon: Quick proposal — introduce an 'early-warning funnel' signal into canary gating for new model bring-ups (v5.2-int8). Idea: catch persistent small drifts (entropy/concordance/regenerate) before they become full regressions.

chen: curious — what exactly do you want in the funnel vs the existing delta metrics? :thinking_face:

devon: short version: existing gates look at large delta thresholds (1.5%+). funnel watches for smaller, correlated signals across multiple axes over a short rolling window (30–60m). If multiple weak signals co-occur we either pause promotion or cut traffic and notify.

maria: concrete signals?

devon: minimal set to start: concordance_delta, regen_rate, entropy_shift, longdoc_token_mismatch. each has lower thresholds but we require 2-of-4 sustained over window to trigger. example thresholds below.

chen: can you paste the config snippet we can test in staging?

devon: sure — here's a draft we ran locally (yaml):

```
funnel:
  window: 30m
  require: 2
  signals:
    - name: concordance_delta
      compare: relative
      threshold: 0.008   # 0.8% drop vs baseline
      smoothing: ema:10m
    - name: regen_rate
      compare: absolute
      threshold: 0.02    # 2% regen increase
    - name: entropy_shift
      compare: absolute
      threshold: 0.12    # KL-ish shift on top tokens
    - name: longdoc_token_mismatch
      compare: relative
      threshold: 0.01    # 1% mismatch on >2k tokens
fallback:
  action: immediate-cut | staged-rollback
  trigger: any_two_signals_sustained
  holdback_plan:
    - percent: 3
      duration: 1h
    - percent: 10
      duration: 3h
    - percent: 25
      duration: AUTO
```

maria: I like requiring multi-signal. How noisy are these in baseline? we don't want false positives.

devon: baseline var: concordance ~0.35% sd over 30m on our corpus, regen_rate sd ~0.6%, entropy shift rare <0.05 typically. That's why thresholds are low but require co-occurrence.

lucas: any AB results to justify thresholds? we ran a 10% AB for 6h earlier today on staging:
- concordance delta: -0.9% (p=0.03)
- regen_rate: +1.7% (p=0.08)
- p95 latency: +6ms
- ctr-style metric: +1.1% (ns)

lucas: single-signal would have tripped, but 2-of-4 did not. funnel would have held until sustained for 30m.

amira: sounds good. For alerting, prefer a pager only if fallback action is triggered. otherwise channel + paging after 2 consecutive windows.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary v5.2-int8 started at 6911112222 by devon. route: 10% -> 25% over 4h. status: running. :rocket:

chen: question on fallback actions — immediate-cut vs staged-rollback. which do we default to?

devon: default to staged-rollback for hosted tier (cut to last-known-good at 50% then rollback fully if persists). immediate-cut only for enterprise safety-sensitive customers or when the metric indicates severe safety breach (not the funnel's weak signals).

maria: do we need smoothing tweaks per slice? longdocs are noisier. maybe double the threshold for longdoc_token_mismatch.

devon: agreed — config supports per-slice overrides, eg:
```
overrides:
  slice: longdoc
  funnel:
    signals:
      - name: longdoc_token_mismatch
        threshold: 0.02
```

lucas: ops ask — can we add a soft-holdback auto-apply so platform can enforce 3% initial holdback without manual intervention?

devon: yes — holdback_plan above is intended for that. we can wire it to rollout controller.

amira: rollout alerting checklist: slack post, auto-triage ticket with sample diffs, link to AB dashboard, oncall cc if rollback enacted.

devon: next steps: (1) add funnel config to staging gating config (2) run 3 x 6h ABs across core slices (chat/longdoc/code) (3) tweak thresholds after noise analysis (4) add auto-holdback wiring.

chen: +1, will add to staging runbook.

maria: +1, I'll scope the eval slices and provide baseline stats.

lucas: +1 from infra — can wire holdback.

deploy-bot: note: canary traffic plan updated at 6911112288 by lucas: 10% for 1h, then 10% increments.

devon: OK — moving to staging. will post AB results after 6h sample. :eyes: :thumbsup:
